text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Trade unions in the mining sector signed agreement with the government to cooperate in projects related to the sector's restructuring..
- Romania will pay its communist-era debts worth $7.8 million to Poland in two tranches, the paper says.
- Within the next 10 days Romania will send 400 peace-keepers to U.N. multi-national force to guard food and aid deliveries in Albania.
- The new round of bilateral treaty talks with Ukraine failed to set some details. The neighbours have decided to meet again after ironing out divergences on those articles.
- A teenager was killed in the northeast city of Iasi by his friend, after he was kidnapped.
- Jean-Marie Le Pen, leader of France's far-right National Front said he wants to visit Romania, the paper said.
- The trial of Jiu Valley coalminers' leader Miron Cosma could last up to 20 years, the newspaper quoted one prosecutor as saying. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
